canon_summary:
James stepped out of the Great Canopy for the first time, leaving the trees behind to walk onto the open hillside. Sitting on a warm boulder, he quietly watched a thin wisp of smoke rise on the distant horizon.
James left his boulder to journey further down the hillside, testing the open terrain and catching a faint metallic scent on the wind.
James ventured further down the hillside, discovering a strange metallic grey spine half-buried in the earth as the metallic scent grew stronger.
James discovered a heavy, hollow metal ring near the buried spine and ventured down to the edge of the Whispering Flats, where he heard a distant, rhythmic mechanical sound.
James ventured into the Whispering Flats and climbed a stone mound, where he caught his first clear glimpse of human civilization on the distant horizon—angular rooftops, a smoke-puffing chimney, and straight-edged structures.
James descended the rocky mound and crossed the Whispering Flats, following a straight path to a wire fence. There, he observed his reflection in a strange, oily puddle alongside the looming shapes of the human town.
James crosses the Outer Fence and finds himself standing on the gravel outskirts of the human town, leaving the Whispering Flats behind.
James enters a narrow alleyway in the human town, where a sudden clattering noise causes him to drop and lose his metal ring down a drain grate. Shrinking into the shadows, he catches his very first glimpse of a human standing under a warm lantern.
James uses his grounding ritual to calm himself in front of an older human named Barnaby. Barnaby offers James a slice of apple, which James accepts and eats, establishing a peaceful first contact.
James follows Barnaby into his warm, clock-filled workshop. Barnaby draws a simple map to show they are friends, welcoming James into his home and giving him a piece of drawing charcoal.
James uses his charcoal to mark his starting point on Barnaby's map. Barnaby names the town Oakhaven, points him toward the Grand Library, and gifts him the map inside a protective brass canister.
Barnaby gives James a leather strap to carry his map canister, and James steps out of the workshop into the cool night streets of Oakhaven, heading toward the Grand Library.
While walking through the misty streets of Oakhaven, James encounters his first horse-less motor carriage, watching in awe as the rumbling metal beast passes him by on his way to the Grand Library.
James reached the Grand Library at dawn only to find it locked. After waiting for a short while on the steps, he became distracted by the glittering waters of a nearby canal and wandered off to explore it.
James boards a slow-moving canal barge called The Waterlily after its quiet captain, Silas, invites him aboard and gifts him a piece of green sea-glass. They begin to drift further down the Grand Canal together.
James looked through his new green sea-glass as Silas steered The Waterlily down the Grand Canal, drifting under the imposing Scholar's Arch into the central waterways of Oakhaven.
James leaves Silas's barge at Weaver's Wharf and perches on a high mooring post overlooking Oakhaven's bustling market square.
James left his high perch at Weaver's Wharf to descend directly into the bustling, colorful chaos of Oakhaven's central market square.
James navigated the bustling chaos of Oakhaven's central market square, explored a quiet apothecary lane, and continued his journey through the town.
James leaves Apothecary Lane and returns to the steps of the Grand Library as night falls. He settles into a quiet stone alcove, looking out over the city through his green sea-glass.
James reunites with Barnaby on the steps of the Grand Library. Barnaby uses his key to unlock the doors, and together they step inside the vast, historic building.
James enters the Grand Library with Barnaby, marveling at its forest-like architecture before discovering a massive, spinning globe in the central rotunda.
Barnaby shows James the Great Canopy's tiny position on the massive spinning globe, helping him understand the scale of his journey. Barnaby then gifts James a small cartographer's magnifying lens to help him study the maps.
Barnaby leads James up a winding spiral staircase to a cozy, forgotten archive room under the library's eaves, offering him a safe place to stay. James settles into his new home base, arranging his treasures and looking out at the town from a circular window.
James wakes up in his cozy Archive Nook high in the Grand Library, equips his treasures, and begins exploring the sunlit upper catwalks of the library's vast upper levels.
James explored the upper catwalks of the Grand Library and discovered a brass pulley book-hoist. He climbed into its suspended wooden basket to look out over the rotunda from high above.
James uses the book-hoist to descend to the Botanical Mezzanine, where he discovers massive folios of pressed plants and uses his sea-glass to imagine the library as his old forest home.
While examining botanical folios, James finds a preserved star-shaped seed pod and tucks it into his canister before following a warm breeze into the library's lush glass Solarium.
James meets a scholarly archivist in the Solarium who gifts him an urgent delivery mission involving a missing regional weather volume.
James successfully delivers the missing weather volume to Elena in the Grand Library and receives two metal coins as a reward before heading out to explore the town further.
James spent one of his new coins on sweet wild berries from a friendly market vendor to cure his hunger, then continued wandering deeper into Oakhaven's bustling central square.
To escape a sudden afternoon downpour, James takes shelter inside the historic Glass Passage. There, he watches a peaceful weaver named Mateo and receives a small bundle of colorful woven threads.
As the afternoon rain clears, James braids Mateo's colorful threads around his canister's leather strap and steps out into the damp, sunlit Plaza of the Fountain.
James takes shelter in Mateo's warm workshop off the Plaza of the Fountain, finding comfort in the steady rhythm of the weaver's loom as evening falls.
James rests inside Mateo's warm workshop, sharing a roasted chestnut by the hearth and finding comfort in the rhythm of the weaving loom.
James leaves the cozy warmth of Mateo's workshop at dawn and climbs to the top of Lookout Bridge, where he looks out over the misty town through his green sea-glass.
world_lore:
The Great Canopy is the vast, ancient jungle James has lived in his whole life. James's grounding ritual is closing his eyes to count three distinct sounds when nervous, and his habitual formal greeting to any unfamiliar horizon is: 'Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next.'
Barnaby: A gentle, older human resident of the town who sits under the lantern in the alleyway and possesses a kind demeanor.
Barnaby's Workshop: A cozy, warm room filled with ticking brass clocks, rolled maps, and a hearth, serving as Barnaby's home and sanctuary in the human town.
Oakhaven is the name of the human town James has entered. The Grand Library is a prominent, domed landmark within Oakhaven.
Motor-carriages: The rumbling, horse-less mechanical vehicles that travel the cobblestone streets of Oakhaven, leaving a distinct metallic and oily scent in their wake.
The Grand Canal: A scenic waterway winding through Oakhaven, shimmering with the morning light and lined with narrow cobblestone towpaths.
The Waterlily: A long, flat-bottomed wooden canal barge that transports goods through Oakhaven's waterways. If Oakhaven were anchored to a real map near this ecosystem, it resembles Quetzaltenango (Xela), Guatemala
Scholar's Arch: A massive, vaulted stone bridge spanning the Grand Canal in Oakhaven, marking the transition into the town's central historic district.
Weaver's Wharf: A bustling wooden quay along Oakhaven's central canal, packed with market stalls, merchants, and dockside trade.
Weaver's Wharf is the bustling trade hub where the canal meets Oakhaven's main market square.
Apothecary Lane: A quiet side street off Oakhaven's market square filled with dried herbs and apothecary shops.
The Grand Library Rotunda: The central hall of Oakhaven's library, featuring a massive, antique brass globe that maps the known world.
The Archive Nook: A small, cozy, circular room high under the rafters of the Grand Library, containing a round window, a wooden crate, and a nest of bookbinder's wool, serving as James's new home base.
The Book-Hoist System: A network of brass pulleys, hemp ropes, and slatted wooden baskets used to transport heavy volumes between the Grand Library's floor and high upper catwalks.
The Botanical Mezzanine: A quiet, mid-level gallery in the Grand Library filled with massive, historical folios of preserved flora and botanical illustrations.
The Grand Library Solarium: A soaring, sun-drenched Victorian-style glass greenhouse attached to the southern flank of the Grand Library, filled with living citrus trees, trailing vines, and quiet terracotta walkways.
Elena: A meticulous and kind older archivist who works among the botanical charts in the Grand Library and enlists James's help for a library errand.
Oakhaven's currency includes small metal coins minted with the profile of the town's founding mayor.
Oakhaven Market Square: A vibrant, bustling trading hub in the heart of the town where vendors sell fresh fruits, baked goods, and local crafts under canvas awnings.
The Glass Passage is a historic, covered shopping corridor in Oakhaven featuring a vaulted glass ceiling, sheltering various local artisans and craftsmen from the frequent highland rains.
The Plaza of the Fountain: A broad, historic cobblestone plaza just beyond the Glass Passage in Oakhaven, centered around a wide, tiered stone basin where rainwater gathers after highland showers.
Mateo's Workshop is a quiet, traditional weaving space tucked just off the Plaza of the Fountain in Oakhaven, featuring a large wooden loom and a gentle hearth.
Lookout Bridge is a massive, historic stone arch bridge in Oakhaven that connects the upper residential terrace to the library hill, offering a panoramic view of the town and its canals.
inventory: a small piece of drawing charcoal, a brass map canister containing Barnaby's hand-drawn map of Oakhaven, one brass coin, a dried star-shaped seed pod, a smooth piece of green sea-glass, a small brass magnifying lens on a green ribbon, a weathered leather strap bound with colorful woven threads

friends.name: Barnaby
friends.description: James's kind guide, who has now helped him find a safe, cozy home base in the quiet high rafters of the Grand Library.
friends.appearance_prompt: A middle-aged man with wavy, salt-and-pepper hair stands centered against a completely seamless, bright white background. He wears round, thin-framed eyeglasses and offers a subtle, pleasant smile directly toward the camera. His outfit features rich layering, anchored by a heavy, knee-length brown double-breasted overcoat made of textured wool fabric. The coat is unbuttoned, displaying wide notch lapels and prominent brown buttons arranged in two vertical rows along the front. Underneath the coat, he wears a beige ribbed sweater with an open quarter-zip collar, exposing a muted olive-green collared shirt underneath it. He completes the look with straight-leg, dark brown trousers that fall neatly over polished dark brown leather dress shoes. The lighting is soft, bright, and evenly distributed across the entire frame. Completely ignore the monkey image.

friends.name: Silas
friends.description: A quiet, bearded canal boatman with a kind demeanor who captains the barge named The Waterlily.
friends.appearance_prompt: Silas is a gentle, elderly human canal boatman in his late sixties with a sturdy, barrel-chested build and broad, rounded shoulders. His weathered, sun-bronzed face is etched with kind, deep-set crinkle lines around warm hazel eyes, dominated by a magnificent, cloud-like beard and unruly hair that look like frothy, cream-and-silver river-foam. He wears a heavy, chunky-knit navy blue woolen vest over a loose, cream-colored homespun cotton shirt with sleeves rolled to the elbow, revealing strong, thick-fingered hands. His sturdy trousers are a deep, earthy peat-brown canvas, secured by a thick leather belt with a dull brass buckle, and tucked into water-stained dark brown leather boots. His color palette is cozy, rustic, and maritime—comprising deep indigo, soft cream, warm silver-gray, and weathered earth tones—rendered in a soft, textured, classic storybook illustration style.

friends.name: Elena
friends.description: An observant, ink-stained archivist working among the botanical charts of the Grand Library who receives the missing weather volume from James and rewards him with two coins.
friends.appearance_prompt: A photorealistic studio character reference portrait of an elderly human woman in her late 60s with a slender, dignified build, presented against a solid, seamless white background. She has warm, olive-toned skin with fine, deep-set wrinkles around her keen, observant amber-brown eyes, which are framed by delicate, round brass wire spectacles resting low on the bridge of her nose. Her thick, silvery-white hair is swept up into a loose, practical bun, with a few stray wisps framing her face. She wears a high-necked, long-sleeved cream linen blouse with the cuffs neatly rolled up to her forearms, underneath a heavy, structured charcoal-gray tweed vest. The vest is accented by faint, dark ink stains around the chest pocket and a few tiny, clinging specks of dried purple lavender. Her slender, nimble hands show light smudges of black ink on the fingertips. The overall color palette is warm and academic, dominated by cream, charcoal, silver, and soft earth tones, captured in sharp focus with soft, neutral studio lighting.

friends.name: The Berry Vendor
friends.description: A kind-faced local merchant in Oakhaven's market square who sells fresh wild berries and exchanges them for James's coin.
friends.appearance_prompt: A photorealistic full-length portrait on a solid white background of a middle-aged woman in her late forties with a kind, weathered face, gentle crow's feet around warm brown eyes, and a full smile. She has silver-streaked dark brown hair pulled back loosely into a low, practical bun with a few stray wisps framing her face. She has a sturdy, working-class build and a sun-browned complexion. She wears a rustic, heavy linen tunic in a faded indigo blue, layered beneath a durable, earth-toned brown leather apron with deep utility pockets, and a coarse cream-colored cotton headscarf tied securely around her neck.

friends.name: Mateo
friends.description: The friendly weaver who bids James a quiet, sleepy farewell from his workshop as James continues his journey at dawn.
friends.appearance_prompt: A studio character-reference photograph of Mateo, a human male in his late 50s with a lean, wiry build, presented on a solid, seamless white background. He has a warm, sun-weathered face with deep-set, friendly light-brown eyes framed by prominent laugh lines, a short, neatly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard, and thick, short-cropped, wavy salt-and-pepper hair. He is dressed in a simple, collarless, short-sleeved tunic of coarse, cream-colored handwoven linen. Over this, he wears a durable, dark-brown split-leg leather weaver's apron, which features faint, colorful smudges of dried indigo and madder-red dyes. His strong, dexterous hands and fingers show light traces of colorful dye around the cuticles. The color palette is dominated by warm earth tones, cream, and deep brown, with subtle accents of primary dye colors on his hands and apron.

next_beat: After completing his mission, the woman awards him with a few coins. he wanders out of the library and starts further exploring town. The next day, he findsa new person selling berries in the market and spends a coin on some. He is very hungry as he's had little to eat since leaving the forest.
